items.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Mathematical Physics (Senior Research Associate) (1286-26)
items.description:
Lancaster University’s School of Physics and Astronomy is seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate (Senior Research Associate) as part of the John Templeton Foundation award “Open Quantum Systems  and the Causal Structure of Reality”.   The Open Systems collaboration will apply formal, physical and conceptional innovations from the study of open quantum systems to systems without fixed causal structure. Quantum models of the universe feature non-fixed causal structure in terms of dynamical and, in some cases, emergent spacetime structure. Quantum cosmology offers the most general and challenging arena for the open systems approach to physics and metaphysics, since the standard assumption is that the universe is subject to closed quantum dynamics. Fundamental reality is standardly understood by philosophers and scientists to be whatever provides the basis for everything.  The Postdoctoral Research Associate will lead their own research program, and be encouraged to work in this area on issues regarding general relativity and cosmology contributing to questions of the role of scale in general relativity, the emergence of temporal structure, the use of quantum reference frames or other related issues.   The Postdoctoral Research Associate post is full time, funded for 24 months from 1 st  July 2027. In conjunction with the standard application process, please upload a CV and also a writing sample of either a) your best published work or b) single thesis chapter (in the latter case, 30 pages maximum inclusive of references) with your application.  If you have any queries regarding this position, please contact David Sloan at d.sloan@lancaster.ac.uk

items.title: Senior Research Associate in Infectious Disease Epidemiology (1224-26)
items.description:
We are seeking to appoint a full-time Research Associate or Senior Research Associate  until March 2029, with the possibility of further extension.  This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing research programme using real-world contact data and mathematical modelling to understand how infectious diseases spread and the potential impact of different control measures. The work will focus predominantly on two uniquely rich datasets, one capturing general population contact patterns during the COVID-19 pandemic using large-scale contact tracing data, and one focused specifically on school-aged children, to help shape public health policy on disease control both in schools and more broadly. The successful candidate will join Lancaster Medical School and work closely with Dr Jonathan Read and Dr Trystan Leng.  We welcome applications from researchers with a PhD in (or equivalent experience) in infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical modelling, quantitative social science, or a related discipline. The postholder will clean and analyse contact patterns from two distinct datasets: 1) the NHS/UKHSA contact tracing data from England, collected during the COVID-19 pandemic and 2) data collected from the School and Community Connections study, a bespoke study which will collect data specifically for this analysis, aimed at understanding the contact patterns of schoolchildren. Further, the postholder will use transmission-dynamic models informed by this contact data alongside surveillance data, fitted using Bayesian methods, to undertake scenario-based mathematical modelling of the potential impact of a range of public health interventions, as well as exploring the usefulness of contact data in explaining observed patterns of incidence.  Depending on experience, the postholder may also contribute to survey design and data collection during the School and Community Connections Study.  The post is funded jointly through a MRC grant awarded to Dr Read and through Dr Leng's Wellcome Early Career Award 'Control without closure: school-level approaches for pathogen control within and between schools':  https://wellcome.org/research-funding/funding-portfolio/funded-grants/control-without-closure-school-level-approaches   You will liaise with colleagues within Lancaster Medical School (Dr Sam Moore) alongside external partners, including Prof Henrik Salje (University of Cambridge), Prof Moritz Kraemer (University of Oxford), colleagues at UKHSA, and the UK government’s Department for Education science team.  You will be expected to be based at Lancaster University, however, we can consider remote working within the UK. There is also the opportunity for a longer-term research visit to external partners’ institutions.  We welcome applications from candidates seeking flexible working requests.  You will join a top 10-UK university in the Complete University Guide 2027 situated in a vibrant research environment. Lancaster Medical School, within the Faculty of Health and Medicine (FHM) at Lancaster University, provides a friendly research environment that strongly supports the individual needs of each employee and which actively promotes a healthy work-life balance. FHM is committed to family-friendly and flexible working policies and has held a Silver Athena SWAN award since 2014 in recognition of its good employment practice undertaken to address gender equality in higher education and research.  For more information, please contact:  Dr Jonathan Read:  Jonathan.read@lancaster.ac.uk   Dr Trystan Leng,  t.leng@lancaster.ac.uk   The post is available from 1 st  January 2027.

items.description:
Job Title: Senior/ Research Associate in Plant Biochemistry   Contract: Indefinite with end date (currently 31/08/2028)   Position Summary:   Applications are invited for a postdoctoral researcher in Plant Biochemistry within the  Lancaster Photosynthesis team  under the supervision of Dr Doug Orr. This new position will join the Plant Biology grouping within the Lancaster Environment Centre, which consists of roughly 35 people including PIs, postdoctoral researchers, research technicians and postgraduate students.  This is part of a BBSRC-funded project that focuses on improving our understanding of Rubisco activity, and pursuing a novel target for increasing Rubisco activity in plants and cyanobacteria. This project is in collaboration with Prof. Martin Cann at Durham University. At Lancaster we will focus on understanding Rubisco activity of recombinant proteins  in vitro , and testing these  in planta  to understand the impact of mutations on leaf level photosynthesis.  The ideal candidate for this position in Plant Biochemistry will have a genuine interest and the curiosity to pursue new research avenues in Rubisco. With training and support, you will be responsible for leading  in vitro  and  in vivo  research to advance the understanding of Rubisco activity. You will lead the molecular and biochemical study of novel Rubisco variants to build fundamental understanding, and lead the physiological characterisation of plants expressing these proteins. You will design and carry out experimental and computational work, analyse data, present results in oral and written form and lead the preparation of scientific manuscripts.  You will join the collaborative and supportive  Lancaster Photosynthesis team  and have access to state-of-the-art resources, including a well-equipped lab for plant molecular biology and biochemistry work using ionising radiation, high-specification plant growth chambers, and the Lancaster High End Computing (HEC) Cluster. Professional development opportunities and training courses to broaden your expertise and skills will be encouraged and are covered by the project.  Individuals from all diversity groups are encouraged to apply. LEC offers a collegial and stimulating environment for career development, based on departmental values and embedded Equality, Diversity and Inclusivity (EDI) considerations and actions. We are committed to family-friendly and flexible working policies on an individual basis, as well as the Athena SWAN Charter, which recognises and celebrates good employment practice undertaken to address gender equality in higher education and research. Furthermore, we are active and progressive around sustainability, wellbeing and social justice agendas.      Timeframe:   This position is available for immediate start, with candidates ideally available to start by early 2027, however this is negotiable.  You will join us on an indefinite contract however the role remains contingent on external funding. This position will initially have an end date of 30/08/2028, with the possibility for extension.  We anticipate interviews will be held within 3 weeks of the closing date, with decisions communicated 1-2 weeks after the interview date.      To apply for this post:   In reading your application documents, we are assessing if you are a good fit to this position and if this position is a good fit for you. To be able to do this, we need you to tell us about your expertise and experience to date, and your research interests. We want to know about the skills you had the opportunity to develop, put within the context of your previous study/work environment by, for example, briefly describing the research facilities available to you, and whether you had opportunities to attend conferences/scientific meetings and develop transferable skills. Please let us know if you have had a career break for any reason so that we can consider the achievements listed on your CV, including your publication record, in relation to these factors.   There is flexibility to appoint either a junior (grade 6) or senior (grade 7) postdoc to this role, with responsibilities and salary set accordingly, and dependent on the successful candidate’s current expertise and experience level.      What to include in each section of your application?    Cover letter:  Please discuss why you are interested in this position, your career goals, and how you anticipate this position will help you achieve those goals. Please also describe the skills you have developed that are relevant to this post and tell us about any skills you want to develop further. It is helpful for us to know your contribution toward the achievements and experiences listed on your CV that are relevant to this post.   CV:  Please include the following sections: Scientific interests; Education history; Professional experience/Employment history; Areas of expertise/Skills; Publications; Presentations.  And, if applicable: Honours/Awards/Prizes/Funding (e.g. travel grant, best poster); Academic service (e.g. review of manuscripts); Outreach; Career development (e.g. training courses or workshops).   Supporting Statements:  Please provide a supporting statement for each criterium in the Personal Specification document that is listed as being scored via “Supporting Statements”. This should include examples that provide evidence of your experience and expertise. Aim for one paragraph per criterium (~50-200 words).   Referees:  Contact information for at least two referees.      For informal enquiries relating to this post, please contact:   Dr Doug Orr  d.j.orr@lancaster.ac.uk .  Further details on our research and team are available here:   http://wp.lancs.ac.uk/lancsphotosynthesis/    https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/lec/about-us/people/douglas-orr

items.title: Senior Research Associate (1137-26)
items.description:
The School of Mathematical Sciences at Lancaster University invites applications for a three-year postdoctoral position to work on the EPSRC-funded project  “ Mutations and geometric models”. The Principal Investigator is Dr Coelho Simões.   Calabi-Yau (CY) triangulated categories are ubiquitous in mathematics, particularly in geometry and representation theory. Due to their physical origin, n-CY categories have been extensively studied for n=2,3. However, as a homological condition, the n-CY property can be studied for any integer n meaning there are many more examples: categories naturally arising in modular representation theory, singularity theory, Fuss-Catalan combinatorics, and higher homological algebra are n-CY for n different from 2 and 3. The systematic study of CY categories in these wider contexts is in its infancy and many aspects remain poorly understood. The main aim of the project seeks to provide methods to address this shortfall using mutations and geometric models.  The successful candidate is expected to hold a PhD degree in mathematics or a related discipline, with specialism in one of the fields of homological algebra, representation theory or algebraic combinatorics. Expertise in triangulated categories, representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras, combinatorial/geometric models arising from surfaces, singularity theory or modular representation theory is highly desirable. You will be expected to learn quickly, engage with new ideas, and contribute new insights.  This work will take place in our thriving Pure Mathematics section, which has considerable expertise in algebra, geometry, analysis, probability, and discrete mathematics. Lancaster is one of the UK’s top mathematical science departments, ranked 7th in the most recent Research Excellence Framework, and joint 1st for the impact of its research. The School, which holds an Athena SWAN Bronze Award, strives to provide a supportive and friendly environment for early career researchers, and offers a comprehensive career development programme. You will be able to focus on your research as the post carries no teaching or administrative duties. Teaching experience will be available on a voluntary basis should you wish to gain teaching experience. You will be encouraged to conduct research visits and will have access to travel funds to do so.   The position starts on 1st February 2027 (or as soon as possible after), for up to 36 months. When applying, in addition to completing the online application, candidates should attach a full CV, a cover letter, a 1-page research statement describing how your expertise is relevant to this position and your future research plans, and the details of two referees. Interviews will take place in December and will be conducted online.  Please contact Dr Raquel Coelho Simões (   r.coelhosimoes@lancaster.ac.uk ) for further information or to discuss the post informally.

items.description:
The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research.   We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee.    Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference.   The role   We are seeking a talented and ambitious postdoctoral researcher to join our thriving research community as a Research Development Fellow. This new position offers an exciting opportunity to build your own research profile while playing a key role in developing high-quality, impactful research with your Discipline and across the School of Social Sciences. As a Research Development Fellow, you will work at the heart of our research community, bringing together academic expertise, external partnerships and funding opportunities to support the development of ambitious research programmes. You will collaborate with researchers across Politics, International Relations, Sociology, Criminology and Media and Communications helping colleagues secure external funding, generate impactful research and address major business and societal challenges. Working closely with academics, doctoral researchers and external partners, you will help create research programmes that deliver meaningful impact for organisations, policymakers and society. Build collaborations across disciplines, faculties and external organisations.  Contribute methodological and intellectual expertise to research projects and funding proposals.  Support the creation of impactful research addressing industrial priorities, economic growth and societal challenges.  Publish high-quality research and contribute to a growing body of evidence that influences practice and policy.   Importantly, up to  20% of your workload will be protected for your own independent research , enabling you to build your research profile, develop publications and pursue your academic interests alongside collaborative projects.   About You   We are looking for proactive, collaborative researchers who are excited by both generating excellent research and enabling others to do the same.  You will have:   A PhD in politics, industrial relations, criminology, sociology, media and communications or another closely related discipline, completed by the appointment start date.  The ability to develop innovative research ideas, robust study designs and compelling funding proposals.  Strong research and methodological capability appropriate to the relevant disciplines, including theoretical, qualitative, quantitative, comparative, empirical, computational, mixed-methods or participatory approaches, as relevant, and proficiency in appropriate analytical tools or programming languages.  Excellent communication, relationship-building and project coordination skills.  A developing research profile with evidence of high-quality publications or a strong publication pipeline.  A commitment to research integrity, collaboration and inclusive research culture.   We welcome applications from researchers with expertise in areas addressed by current members of research staff including:   European and British politics   Contemporary geopolitics  Public policy  Criminology and criminal justice  Digital societies  Inequalities and diversities  Families and the life course  Wellbeing  Media and communication  Sustainability    How to apply   To apply, please upload a CV and cover letter along with your application to the University website. Please detail the below in your covering letter.   How your research agenda addresses significant research challenges in Politics, International Relations, Sociology, Criminology and Media and Communications (or a combination of these) and how it aligns with the current research interests of academics in the Departments of Politics and Sociology at Surrey.   The research methodologies you can draw on, with examples of how you have used them.   Your understanding of the research funding landscape in your discipline and in the wider disciplines in the School of Social Science.   Your experience of contributing to funding applications, externally funded projects or multi-partner research collaborations   Inquiries should be addressed to Professor Jo Blanden,  J.Blanden@surrey.ac.uk .   Interviews will be held in January.

Work closely with researchers across the LungSight consortium, including Manchester Metropolitan Sheffield, Cambridge, Leicester and Leeds Universities, as well as clinical, NHS, patient/public and third-sector partners; participate in project meetings, joint research activities and dissemination. Based at University Hospital Southampton, you will investigate why individuals with similar levels of adiposity differ substantially in their risk of developing type 2 diabetes and its complications. Conduct genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of obesity-related traits, adiposity phenotypes and metabolic outcomes using large-scale genetic and epidemiological datasets.  Apply Mendelian randomisation and complementary genetic epidemiological approaches to investigate potential causal relationships between different aspects of adiposity, type 2 diabetes and its complications.  Perform post-GWAS analyses, including fine-mapping, functional annotation, gene prioritisation and pathway enrichment, to identify genes and biological mechanisms underlying obesity-related metabolic risk.  Investigate the genetic determinants of different obesity-related phenotypes and their associations with metabolic and cardiometabolic outcomes.  Contribute to high-quality scientific publications, conference presentations and the dissemination of research findings.  Collaborate with multidisciplinary researchers across genetic epidemiology, statistical genetics, genomics, clinical medicine and data science.    You will have opportunities to develop your expertise in statistical genetics and genetic epidemiology, contribute to innovative analytical approaches and build your publication record within an internationally collaborative research environment.    You will have:     A PhD in genetic epidemiology, statistical genetics, bioinformatics, biostatistics, computational biology or a closely related discipline.  Experience analysing large-scale genetic, genomic or epidemiological datasets, ideally including UK Biobank.  Strong computational skills, including proficiency in R and/or Python and experience working in Linux-based computing environments.  Knowledge of GWAS methodology, including genetic data quality control, association testing and interpretation of results. items.title: Research Fellow in Cell and Developmental Biology (3545826BJ)
items.description:
We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Research Fellow to join the Salah Elias laboratory at the University of Southampton and lead the experimental research within a BBSRC-funded project investigating mechanisms of mammary epithelial morphogenesis through AI-integrated human organoid models and predictive cell fate mapping. This is an excellent opportunity to shape an innovative project and develop a distinctive interdisciplinary profile at the interface of cell and developmental biology, human organoid models, advanced imaging, molecular phenotyping and computational biology.   About the project   The project combines patient-derived mammary organoids, high-resolution 3D/4D imaging, single-cell transcriptomics and AI-driven analysis and modelling to uncover mechanisms governing epithelial morphogenesis. At its core is a fundamental question: how do polarised cell divisions coordinate luminogenesis with cell fate and differentiation to build and maintain functional epithelial architecture? By addressing this question in physiologically relevant human models, the project aims to define how these mechanisms safeguard epithelial integrity and how their disruption leads to abnormal tissue organisation.  You will take a central role in the scientific development of this ambitious programme, including experimental design, data analysis and interpretation. You will use patient-derived human mammary organoids and gene loss-of-function approaches, together with high-resolution 3D/4D fluorescence imaging, fate mapping, advanced quantitative analysis, and single-cell RNA sequencing, to connect molecular and cellular mechanisms with cell fate and tissue architecture.  A major strength of the project is the integration of experimental and computational biology. Working with computational researchers, you will integrate multimodal imaging and transcriptomic data into AI-driven mechanistic and predictive models to determine how changes at the level of individual cells influence tissue-level organisation and function.   About you   You will have a PhD, or be close to completing one, in cell biology, developmental biology, stem cell biology or a related discipline.  You will have strong experimental experience across several relevant areas of cell and developmental biology, which may include organoid or mammalian cell culture, epithelial biology, high-resolution fluorescence microscopy and molecular biology. Experience in advanced automated or semi-automated quantitative image analysis would be particularly valuable. An understanding of computational or mathematical modelling would be advantageous, but is not essential.  You will be a creative and collaborative scientist with a proactive, analytical approach and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research. You should be able to plan and conduct rigorous experiments, interpret data, troubleshoot methods and communicate findings clearly.  Alongside leading the experimental research, you will contribute scientific ideas and interpretation, support collaborative projects, help develop grant proposals, prepare research for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, train colleagues in new methods and advise on scientific protocols. You will bring excellent interpersonal skills and work constructively with colleagues and collaborators across disciplines.   What we offer   You will join a collaborative, multidisciplinary and supportive research environment bringing together expertise in mammary biology, organoids, advanced imaging, single-cell biology, AI and computational modelling. You will have access to state-of-the-art microscopy, flow-cytometry and high-performance computing facilities, multidisciplinary training and career-development opportunities. We support flexible working and a healthy work–life balance, alongside access to the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS), subsidised health and fitness facilities and a range of staff discounts. items.title: Research Fellow in Causal Inference and Ecology (3542326WR)
items.description:
We have an exciting opportunity for a Research Fellow to join the UKRI-funded PRECISE (Precision Ecology for a Changing World) project. Moving beyond average effects, the project will predict site-specific responses to environmental management and restoration, supporting effective conservation decisions.  Based in the School of Geography and Environmental Science at the University of Southampton, you will work with researchers at Southampton, the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH) and the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research (NINA), and international collaborators in statistics, causal inference and ecological modelling. Using benchmark datasets produced through ecological simulations and large observational datasets assembled by project partners, you will investigate how sampling strategies and data characteristics affect the performance of alternative causal-inference and machine-learning workflows. Overview of the Role   Are you a researcher with demonstrable expertise in the analysis of climatological data and the implementation and interpretation of climate model projections? Do you have a demonstrable interest in engaging with stakeholders, particularly in public policy and the financial sector? Do you have a background within climate science?    This project will address the lack of adequate early-warning systems for accelerated climate change and tipping-points, for the insurance sector and more broadly. It also aims to address an associated challenge for the insurance sector, given its criticality to the global economy, by helping the sector understand the stressors, and adaptation responses to those stressors, it is likely to face in the coming decades due to the combined effects of climate change, the transition to a net zero economy including regulatory challenges, and potential geopolitical threats.  Through this work, in collaboration with the insurance and reinsurance industry, the successful candidate will help to develop and test a novel early-warning system for accelerating climate change and tipping-points, with aim of informing policy and wider society that unmanageable levels of climate change, with different modalities of climate impacts, are approaching.  This approach draws on ideas from climate attribution and optimal fingerprinting and from economics signal detection but extends this through the application of social science techniques, including decision-gaming and reverse stress testing, by using the insurance sector as a filter to help detect the early signs of an accelerated climate change signal against the background noise of natural variability in the climate.  As part of this early-warning system development, we will produce multi-dimensional storylines using interdisciplinary teams to combine understanding on physical climate change, policy and regulatory changes linked to the net zero transition, and potential geopolitical impacts. items.description:
On the 1 August 2026, The University of Greenwich and the University of Kent formed a pioneering new multi-university group called London and South- East (LASE) University Group.   Should you join us, you will be employed by LASE but will work as part of the University of Kent academic division, contributing to its distinct strengths, community and identity while also being part of a wider group that brings together the scale, resilience and shared ambition of both universities. Through LASE we aim to deliver outstanding education, impactful research, and meaningful regional and global impact.    Do you have the expertise in AI and predictive modelling to help improve how wind turbines operate in icy conditions? If so this role could be ideal.   We’re looking for a Research Associate to join OptimICE, an international Horizon Europe project bringing together 14 organisations to reduce the impact of icing on wind energy in cold climates. This 42-month fixed-term role offers the opportunity to contribute to research that improves how wind turbines are monitored, operated and maintained in icy conditions.  Working closely with Dr Jonathan Nixon and the Kent research team, you’ll develop and validate physics-informed AI models for icing detection and wind-power prediction, helping wind farm operators anticipate icing, predict power production and make better decisions about ice protection and maintenance.   As Research Associate you can expect to be involved in:    Developing and validating physics-informed AI models using turbine, weather and icing-sensor data  Conducting individual and collaborative research, including data collection and analysis  Publishing research findings in peer-reviewed journals and presenting results at conferences  Working with research partners to deliver project objectives and milestones    What will you bring to the role?    A relevant postgraduate degree (Master’s or PhD), a PhD close to submission, or equivalent relevant research experience  Experience conducting research projects, including data collection and analysis  Specialist expertise or theoretical knowledge of machine learning, AI and time-series analysis  Familiarity with research methods and tools used in wind energy data analysis and predictive modelling    What we can offer in return:   As a member of our team, you can expect a friendly, open and collaborative working environment and support in your development and wellbeing. You'll enjoy a range of great staff benefits including:   Hybrid working options allowing a flexible blend of office and home working (to be agreed in line with business needs)     43 days' leave per year (personal leave, bank holidays and additional days allocated for the Christmas period, pro rata for part-time staff)  Excellent pension scheme with generous employer contributions  Corporate employee-funded healthcare plan, in partnership with Benenden Health    For informal enquiries about the role, please contact Dr Jonathan Nixon at    j.nixon-104@kent.ac.uk    For more information about what you can look forward to if you join us, visit our dedicated webpage:  Working at Kent   We are ambitious for our people, our communities and the region we serve – join us in making the world a better place. Visit our website for more on who we are:  http://www.kent.ac.uk/about/   Please see the links below to view the full job description and to apply for this post. For further information regarding the application process, please contact  peopleserviceshr@kent.ac.uk  quoting reference number EMP-017-26.
